hypothesis: Allowing depth contact to slide inside finite exposed key tops with soft human depth guidance can improve instrument clearance; actual mesh self constraints are needed beyond different-finger proxies.
ablation: Same measured-size R frame 24, source initialization, score/key commands, anatomy, 120 mm static wrist workspace, actual level-2 skin, human weight 4 and 100×4 plus 80 feasibility iterations per treatment. Hard/soft depth guidance × active self-pair constraints off/on. All four retain the identical final two-triangulation actual self-mesh rejection gate. No neighbor rate constraints in static planning.
scope: Exploratory static sensitivity pilot; not the graph-reviewed connected trajectory comparison

hard_proxy.scope:
Search for a contact waypoint before planning its bounded approach path.

This keeps anatomy, fixed shoulder/arm lengths, actual skin/contact and proxy
finger spacing. Neighbor speed constraints are deliberately absent because no
trajectory is being exported or accepted. Wrist range is a planning workspace,
not an allowed per-frame jump. The waypoint must still pass mesh/mesh and
naturalness review and then be connected within the original motion bounds.

source.scope:
Audit self/interhand crossings of Blender's actual level-2 skin triangles.

Run in Blender for its CPU BVH, without rendering:
  blender -b --factory-startup -P lab/skin_mesh_audit.py -- INPUT.json OUT.json

All same-hand faces, palm/webbing and forearms participate. Only intersection
confined to a genuinely shared topological feature is exempted. A clear surface
intersection result is not a volume-containment, positive-distance or CCD proof;
body/costume/drum meshes still need inclusion in the complete rig gate.
exclusions: volume containment of open skin surfaces

supersedes: Earlier local accepted poses covered instrument, finite support, bounds and proxy spacing. They now fail actual same-hand skin clearance and cannot be called complete-hand passes.
conclusion: Soft depth guidance reduces instrument depth from roughly 3.04 mm to 0.0147 mm, but neither treatment clears instrument triangles, finger proxies, full self surfaces and all four anchors. Active self constraints do not resolve the folds within this budget. Every numerical trial is rejected.
next_hypotheses: Distinguish pose-induced folds from skin binding/deformation behavior with identical frozen poses.
Evaluate worst individual joint angles, not only aggregate reference deviation.
Plan connected contact/wrist paths with original motion limits and immutable musical ledger.
Replace drummer grip proxies with independently audited hand/body/shell geometry.
